Calcium-mediated amplification of injury

Cultured hepatocytes exposed to an ischemic insult develop a sustained elevation of cytosolic calcium. Investigators then detect membrane phospholipid breakdown and degradation of cytoskeletal proteins before extensive cell rupture. Which calcium-dependent effect best explains these linked findings?

  1. Activation of phospholipases and proteases
  2. Inhibition of all intracellular hydrolases
  3. Selective stimulation of collagen cross-linking
  4. Permanent inactivation of endonucleases
  5. Restoration of mitochondrial ATP stores
Answer and explanation

Activation of phospholipases and proteases

These enzymes damage membranes and structural proteins, amplifying injury.

Option explanations

Activation of phospholipases and proteases: These enzymes damage membranes and structural proteins, amplifying injury.

Inhibition of all intracellular hydrolases: Calcium activates several destructive enzymes instead of inhibiting all of them.

Selective stimulation of collagen cross-linking: Collagen cross-linking is extracellular and does not explain both findings.

Permanent inactivation of endonucleases: Calcium can promote nuclease activity rather than permanently suppress it.

Restoration of mitochondrial ATP stores: Calcium overload can worsen mitochondrial dysfunction.
